technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Shell to implement the shell interface for the Spring Cloud Data Flow REST API.
Leverage Spring Boot ConfigurationProperties to bind module metadata for the 'module info' command.
Port existing Spring XD modules (http, tcp, twitterstream, twittersearch, filter, transform) to Spring Cloud Stream application starters.
Implement each module as a Spring Cloud Stream source or processor with appropriate binder configuration.
Use Maven-based multi-module project structure for organizing the shell and module components.
Follow Spring Cloud Stream functional programming model for module implementation.
assumptions: The developer has prior experience with Spring Cloud Data Flow, Spring Shell, and Spring Cloud Stream.
Existing Spring XD module code can be adapted with minimal refactoring for Spring Cloud Stream compatibility.
REST API endpoints for Spring Cloud Data Flow are already available and stable.
Required dependencies and build tools (Maven, JDK 17+) are pre-configured in the development environment.
Unit and integration testing frameworks are already set up in the project.
Documentation and community resources for Spring XD to Spring Cloud Stream migration are sufficient.

activities.activity_description: Implement shell commands for stream operations using Spring Shell and Spring Cloud Data Flow REST API.
Design and implement ConfigurationProperties-based strategy for module metadata and 'module info' command.
Port the http module from Spring XD to Spring Cloud Stream as a source module.
Port the tcp module from Spring XD to Spring Cloud Stream as a source module.
Port the twitterstream module from Spring XD to Spring Cloud Stream as a source module.
Port the twittersearch module from Spring XD to Spring Cloud Stream as a source module.
Port the filter module from Spring XD to Spring Cloud Stream as a processor module.
Port the transform module from Spring XD to Spring Cloud Stream as a processor module.
Perform integration testing of shell interface and all ported modules with Spring Cloud Data Flow.
